Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In a simple undirected graph [MATH: G=(V,E)] with [MATH: m] vertices [MATH: v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_m] and [MATH: n] edges [MATH: e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_n,] the incidence matrix [MATH: B] is an [MATH: m \times n] matrix (table), where the entry at the intersection of the [MATH: i]th row and the [MATH: j]th column equals:

Content:
- [MATH: 1,] if the vertex [MATH: v_i] is incident to the edge [MATH: e_j;]
- [MATH: 0,] otherwise.

Content:
In multigraphs, each loop contributes [MATH: 2] to the corresponding entry since the edge is incident to the vertex twice.

Content:
As we know, graphs can be represented graphically in various equally valid ways. In contrast, once we have fixed orderings of the vertices and of the edges, the incidence matrix of a graph is unique.

Content:
Consider the graph below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/057a2bace33df8ae5336a7f79be1dd2b]

Content:
Let's examine the vertices [MATH: v_1,v_2,] and [MATH: v_3] of the graph to determine the entries of the incidence matrix.

Content:
- The vertex [MATH: v_1] is incident to the edges [MATH: e_1] and [MATH: e_2.] Hence, we write [MATH: 1] in the [MATH: 1]st and [MATH: 2]nd columns of the [MATH: 1]st row, and [MATH: 0] in the other columns.

Content:
| | [MATH: e_1] | [MATH: e_2] | [MATH: e_3] | [MATH: e_4] |
| [MATH: v_1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 0] |
| [MATH: v_2] | | | | |
| [MATH: v_3] | | | | |

Content:
- The vertex [MATH: v_2] is incident to the edges [MATH: e_1, e_2,] and [MATH: e_3.] Hence, we write [MATH: 1] in the [MATH: 1]st, [MATH: 2]nd, and [MATH: 3]rd columns of the [MATH: 2]nd row, and [MATH: 0] in the [MATH: 4]th column.

Content:

| [MATH: v_1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 0] |
| [MATH: v_2] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 0] |
| [MATH: v_3] | | | | |

Content:
- The vertex [MATH: v_3] is incident to the edge [MATH: e_3] and also to the loop formed by [MATH: e_4.] Hence, we write [MATH: 1] in the [MATH: 3]rd column of the [MATH: 3]rd row, [MATH: 2] in the [MATH: 4]th column to indicate the loop, and [MATH: 0] in the other columns.

Content:

| [MATH: v_1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 0] |
